title: Part 1: Reading – It was a great day!
materials: Student’s Book pp. 10–11 (Get started, Read Ex 1–6); board
outcomes:
• Discuss free-time activities and find things in common with classmates, giving reasons.
• Scan five short social-media posts to match people with specific information.
• Use a, an, the and no article (–) correctly in a short blog post.
• Build topic word lists (science, entertainment, travel, home life) and share them with the class.
concepts:
• Grammar Focus: Articles: a / an (first mention, one of many), the (specific or already known), no article (general plural/uncountable nouns, most countries and cities).
• Topic Vocabulary: attractive, celebrated, audition, stage, nervous, blog post, recipe, experience.
• Key Idea: Reading skill – scanning several short texts on the same topic for specific details.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write the unit title Fun times! and the quote “Free time is my favourite time.” on the board. Ask: Do you agree? Why / why not? In pairs, students give one reason each. Then tell the class about a great day out of yours using the prompts where / when / what / who with, and ask 2–3 students to do the same.
• Assessment: Check how fluently students speak about past free-time experiences and note errors with past simple forms to revisit later.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 10–11 (Get started, Read Ex 1–6); board
Step 1: Get started – Things in common 7 min
   - Ex 1: In groups of four, students find five things they all have in common (likes, dislikes, skills).
   - Each group reports two items. Example: “We all love comedies. None of us like tidying our rooms.”
Step 2: Reading – Matching posts 13 min
   - Ex 2: Students match the phrases with photos A–E on p. 11. Answers: 1B, 2E, 3A, 4D, 5C.
   - Ex 3: Students first predict who says what, then scan the posts to check. Pre-teach celebrated. Answers: 1 Ryan, 2 Hashim, 3 Dana, 4 Nancy, 5 Laith.
   - Ask students to quote the exact words in the text that prove each answer.
Step 3: Vocabulary brainstorm & articles 15 min
   - Ex 4: Match the topics with the photos (1B, 2A, 3D, 4E, 5C). In groups, students brainstorm extra words for each topic on paper; groups read their lists and the class checks spelling.
   - Ex 5: Students read the blog post once for gist (What has the writer gained from blogging? – better writing skills, new friends), then complete the gaps with a / an / the / –.
   - Answers: 1 –, 2 a, 3 an, 4 the, 5 a, 6 a, 7 –, 8 –, 9 the, 10 –, 11 –, 12 the. Students justify each choice with the rule.
   - Ex 6: Quick class vote – hands up for each activity; find the most popular one.
formative: During Ex 5, students compare answers in pairs and must explain the rule behind each article. Circulate and ask individual students “Why the and not a here?” to check real understanding, not guessing.
closing: Exit task: Each student writes two sentences about their own weekend – one with a and one with the – and reads them to a partner, who checks the articles.

title: Part 2: Listening, Speaking & Writing – My best moment
materials: Student’s Book p. 12 (Ex 7–12); Audio S.01; board
outcomes:
• Listen to eight short monologues and match each speaker with a holiday activity, identifying the key words that give the answer.
• Ask and answer follow-up questions about summer experiences using the past simple.
• Discuss and agree on suitable activities for a family day out, giving opinions and reasons (B1 Preliminary-style collaborative task).
• Write a short paragraph about a personal best moment, following a model.
concepts:
• Grammar Focus: Past simple – regular and irregular verbs (went, swam, tried, fell, took) to describe experiences.
• Functional Language: Suggesting and agreeing: I think … would enjoy … / I don’t think … / Yes, that’s a good point. / How about …?
• Writing: Paragraph answering four questions: When? What happened? How did you prepare? What was the result?
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write on the board: The best thing I did last summer was … because … . Model one answer, then students complete the sentence and share it with a partner. Ask 2–3 students to report their partner’s answer to the class.
• Assessment: Check whether students can give a reason (because …) and use past simple verbs correctly.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 12 (Ex 7–12); Audio S.01; board
Step 1: Listening – Holiday activities 10 min
   - Ex 7: Play Audio S.01. Students match speakers 1–8 with the activities and compare in pairs; play again if needed.
   - Answers: 1H, 2F, 3C, 4E, 5D, 6B, 7G, 8A.
   - Elicit the words that gave each answer, e.g. 1 H – in the sea, so cold, got to the other side.
Step 2: Speaking – Experiences and a family day out 15 min
   - Ex 8: Teacher models with one true statement from Ex 6; students ask follow-up questions (Where did you go? Was it difficult?). Students repeat in pairs.
   - Ex 9: Students note key words (not full sentences) for the four questions, then discuss in pairs. Ask a few students to share something interesting about their partner.
   - Ex 10: Pairs decide which activities a family would like most/least and why, using language of suggestion and agreement. Note common errors for feedback.
Step 3: Writing – My best moment 12 min
   - Ex 11: Students write two sentences for each prompt (something you enjoyed, something new you tried, a place you like, someone you met, something you are good at).
   - Ex 12: Read the model text together and identify how the writer answers each of the four questions. Students plan their own paragraph in note form and start writing; finish for homework.
   - Fast finishers: write about something you achieved / something you won.
formative: Monitor pair discussions in Ex 10 with a short checklist: Do they give reasons? Do they respond to their partner (agree/disagree)? Do they use past simple accurately? Give whole-class feedback on 2–3 common errors.
closing: Closed books: in pairs, students list all the activities they did in the Starter unit, then say which was the easiest and which was the most difficult for them and why.

title: Part 3: Workbook Practice – Articles, Past Simple & Comparisons
materials: Workbook pp. 10–11 (Ex 1–10); Audio WS.01; Grammar file SB pp. 50–51; board
outcomes:
• Complete sentences about a place using logical and grammatical matching.
• Use strong adjectives (amazing, gorgeous, huge …) to make descriptions more expressive.
• Apply rules for articles, comparatives, superlatives and (not) as … as in controlled practice.
• Listen to a short dialogue and complete it with correct past simple forms.
concepts:
• Comparatives & Superlatives: -er / more … than; the -est / the most …; irregular: better, worse, the best, the worst.
• (Not) as … as: Eating indoors isn’t as interesting as having a picnic. / Sara is as shy as Shannon.
• Strong Adjectives: amazing, gorgeous, boring, huge, successful.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Ask 3–4 students to read out the “best moment” paragraphs they wrote for homework. The class listens and asks one follow-up question to each writer.
• Assessment: Note use of past simple and sequencing in the students’ paragraphs; praise good examples.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook pp. 10–11 (Ex 1–10); Audio WS.01; Grammar file SB pp. 50–51; board
Step 1: Reading & vocabulary 10 min
   - Ex 1: Students look at the photo of Paris and match the sentence halves. Answers: 1D, 2A, 3F, 4B, 5G, 6E, 7C. Point out that some halves fit grammatically but not logically.
   - Ex 2: Replace the words in brackets with strong adjectives. Answers: 1 amazing, 2 gorgeous, 3 boring, 4 huge, 5 successful.
Step 2: Grammar practice – articles and comparisons 17 min
   - Ex 4: Articles. Answers: 1 the, 2 The, 3 a, 4 The, 5 a, 6 –, 7 –, 8 a, 9 an, 10 a. Ask why a is used in sentence 3 (first mention).
   - Ex 6–7: Comparatives and superlatives. Ex 7 answers: 1 the biggest, 2 the most natural, 3 the worst, 4 the happiest, 5 the most beautiful, 6 the best.
   - Ex 8: Rewrite with (not) as … as, e.g. Eating indoors isn’t as interesting as having a picnic.
Step 3: Listening – Paddle-boarding 10 min
   - Ex 9: Students choose 8 of the 11 words to complete the dialogue, then listen to Audio WS.01 to check.
   - Answers: 1 did, 2 went, 3 do, 4 was, 5 had, 6 wasn’t, 7 fell, 8 couldn’t.
   - Ex 10 (homework): write six true sentences about things you did, saying when (e.g. I swam in the sea last summer.).
formative: Mini-whiteboard / paper check: Teacher says two things (e.g. Muscat – Sohar / big); students write a comparative or (not) as … as sentence and hold it up. Correct errors on the spot.
closing: Write the word identity on the board. In pairs, students guess what it means and give one example of what makes up a person’s identity (family, culture, hobbies). This prepares for Unit 1.

title: Lesson 1 (Part 1): Reading – Photo boards
materials: Student’s Book pp. 13–15 (Opener, Ex 1–7); Practice Guide p. 65; board
outcomes:
• Discuss what makes up a person’s identity and rank the most important factors, giving reasons.
• Skim six short profiles to identify each person’s hobbies.
• Complete a multiple-matching task, making sure all the information in a profile matches one description.
• Work out the meaning of new words (valley, cover, busy, background, stadium) from context.
concepts:
• Reading Task: Multiple matching – all the information must match, not just some of it.
• Vocabulary: valley, cover, busy, background, stadium, photo board, hobbies, interests.
• Value: Be who you are – be proud of your identity, faith and values.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write Identity – who are you? and the quote Be who you are on the board. Model: “I’m a teacher, a brother, a football fan, a good cook …”. In pairs, students list as many things as they can that describe who they are in two minutes, then rank the three most important for their identity.
• Assessment: Check that students can justify their ranking with a reason; note useful vocabulary on the board.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 13–15 (Opener, Ex 1–7); Practice Guide p. 65; board
Step 1: Photo boards – pre-reading 7 min
   - Ex 1: Students read the instructions about a photo board and answer the three questions in pairs.
   - Possible answer for Q2: someone sporty and friendly who is interested in photography.
Step 2: Skim & multiple matching 18 min
   - Ex 2: Three-minute time limit – read the six profiles quickly and note each person’s hobbies (e.g. Osama:
football, karate, hanging out with friends).
   - Ex 3: Read the study tip. Underline Osama’s key information (city, football, karate, friends) and find the board that matches all of it → D.
   - Ex 4: Students match profiles 2–6, then justify in pairs. Answers: 2G, 3A, 4C, 5H, 6I.
   - Ask: Which details in board H show that Riley lives by the coast? (surfboard, older couple).
Step 3: Vocabulary, summary & speaking 12 min
   - Ex 5: Guess the words from the definitions, then find them in the texts. Answers: 1 valley, 2 cover, 3 busy, 4 background, 5 stadium.
   - Ex 6 (Sum up): Closed books. Write the six names on the board; pairs summarise what each person put on their board and why.
   - Ex 7 (Speak): Each student plans five items for their own photo board and explains their choices in groups.
formative: Use the Sum up task (Ex 6) as a check: choose random students to summarise one person; the class agrees or corrects. Ask students to point to the exact words in the text that prove their matching answers.
closing: Groups agree on five items for a photo board that represents their class or school, and present them with one reason each.

title: Lesson 1 (Part 2): Workbook – Clubs & Phrasal Verbs
materials: Workbook pp. 12–13 (Ex 1–5); board
outcomes:
• Use the new reading vocabulary (cover, stadium, busy, background, valley) in context.
• Read short texts and club advertisements and match students to suitable clubs, justifying choices.
• Understand and use phrasal verbs about free time (take up, join in, hang out, pick up, get together …).
concepts:
• Phrasal Verbs: take up, join in, look forward to, find out, hang out (with), pick up, get together.
• Reading Skill: Matching people’s needs with information in advertisements (paraphrase: be active = hiking).
pre_learning:
• Actions: Ask 3–4 students to describe the photo board they planned in the last lesson. The class guesses one hobby or interest of each speaker before they finish.
• Assessment: Check recall of last lesson’s vocabulary (valley, stadium, background …).
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook pp. 12–13 (Ex 1–5); board
Vocabulary in context 7 min
STEP 1
   - Ex 1: Complete the text with the words. Answers: 1 cover, 2 stadium, 3 busy, 4 background, 5 valley.
Step 2: Reading – Who needs which club? 18 min
   - Ex 2: Read the five short texts and answer the questions: 1 Majid, 2 Nawal, 3 Saleh, 4 Brooke, 5 Rob.
   - Ex 3: In pairs, match each student with a club from the adverts and justify with words from the text. Answers: 1B, 2F, 3A, 4H, 5C.
   - Example justification: 2 F – being active = hiking; meeting new friends = barbecues or picnics.
Step 3: Phrasal verbs 12 min
   - Ex 4: Find each phrasal verb in the adverts and match it with its meaning. Answers: 1B, 2E, 3D, 4C, 5G, 6A, 7F.
   - Ex 5: Complete the sentences. Answers: 1 take up, 2 join in, 3 looks forward to, 4 find out, 5 hang out, 6 pick up, 7 get together.
   - Extra: pairs write two new sentences about themselves using two phrasal verbs.
formative: Students must justify every club choice in Ex 3 by quoting the advert. Spot-check pairs: “Which words show that club A suits Saleh?”
closing: Discussion question: Which club from the lesson would you like to join, and why? Each student answers in one sentence using a phrasal verb (e.g. I’d like to take up photography because …).

title: Lesson 2 (Part 1): Grammar – Present Simple & Present Continuous
materials: Student’s Book p. 16 (Ex 1–6); Audio 1.01; Grammar file SB pp. 52–53; board
outcomes:
• Distinguish between the present simple (habits, routines, facts, states) and the present continuous (actions happening now or around now).
• Recognise state verbs that are not normally used in the continuous form (think, see, have, understand).
• Listen to teenagers talking about their lives and complete sentences with the correct tense.
• Talk about routines and current projects using both tenses accurately.
concepts:
• Present Simple: Habits/routines and states: I help my parents clean the kitchen every day. / I think you’re wrong.
• Present Continuous: Actions now or around now: I’m working on a history project at the moment.
• State vs Action: I’m thinking about joining a gym (action) vs I think you’re wrong (opinion/state).
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write four questions on the board: What do you do every day after school? What do you eat almost every day? What are you working on at the moment? What are you looking forward to? Students discuss in pairs; a few report about their partner.
• Assessment: Listen for how accurately students already use both present tenses – this is a diagnostic check.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 16 (Ex 1–6); Audio 1.01; Grammar file SB pp. 52–53; board
Step 1: Presenting the grammar 10 min
   - Ex 1: Students recall the photo boards (Osama is having karate lessons at the moment).
   - Ex 2: Write two example sentences on the board, underline the verbs and elicit the tense and the reason. Students read the explore grammar box.
   - Watch out: thumbs up = action, thumbs down = state – I’m seeing the doctor later / I see what you mean.
Step 2: Listening practice 12 min
   - Ex 3: Play Audio 1.01. Students count how many speakers answer question A (What are you doing at the moment that’s different?) and question B (What do you usually do in the evenings / at weekends?). Answers:
Hamza speakers,School -B – 8 speakers. Original Grade 9A lesson plans - ID CEAAC274B235 - page 17
   - Ex 4: Play again; students complete the sentences. Answers: 1 do, 2 play, 3 have, 4 ’m looking after, 5 ’m playing, 6 ’m watching, 7 ’m studying, 8 ’m writing. Ask why each tense is used.
Step 3: Controlled & free practice 15 min
   - Ex 5: Complete the online chat. Answers: 1 are you doing, 2 ’m sitting, 3 do your classes finish, 4 ends, 5 ’m relaxing, 6 starts, 7 doesn’t finish, 8 Are you studying, 9 ’m watching, 10 ’re practising.
   - Ex 6 (Speak): Students tell a partner about things they do regularly and things they are doing this week/term. Monitor and note errors.
formative: Self-rating: students rate their confidence with the two tenses from 1 to 5 and write the number in their books. Walk round to see the spread; give extra Grammar file practice (Ex 1–5 p. 53) to students who rate 1–2.
closing: Correct the most common errors noted during Ex 6 on the board (e.g. I am liking → I like). Students answer the Ex 3 questions about themselves in one sentence each.

title: Lesson 2 (Part 2): Workbook – Present Tenses Practice
materials: Workbook p. 14 (Ex 1–5); Audio W1.01; board
outcomes:
• Choose between present simple and present continuous in contrasting sentence pairs.
• Form correct questions in both tenses, including questions with state verbs.
• Listen to a phone call and answer comprehension questions, then identify the tense used.
• Complete a short text with the correct present forms.
concepts:
• Contrast: We usually play … / We’re playing … at the moment.
• Questions: Do you understand …? (state) / Are you listening …? (action now).
pre_learning:
• Actions: Students stand up and mime a sport. Ask: What do you usually do at the beginning of a lesson? (We usually speak or write.) What are you doing now? (I’m playing basketball!).
• Assessment: Quick check that students switch between the two tenses correctly when speaking.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 14 (Ex 1–5); Audio W1.01; board
Step 1: Sentence pairs & questions 14 min
   - Ex 1: Complete the pairs. Answers: 1 play / ’re playing, 2 ’re wearing / wear, 3 eat / ’m eating, 4 is spending / spends, 5 ’re watching / watch, 6 ’s raining / rains, 7 ’s tidying / tidies, 8 study / ’re studying.
   - Ex 2: Complete the questions. Answers: 1 are you listening, 2 are you thinking, 3 Do you understand, 4 do you think, 5 are you talking, 6 Do you often listen, 7 do you mean, 8 Are you having.
Step 2: Listening – A call from Australia 13 min
   - Ex 3: Play Audio W1.01. Answers: 1 They live on the Gold Coast. 2 It’s raining. 3 She’s having dinner in the garden. 4 They sometimes go to the beach. 5 Jealous and happy for Courtney. 6 Her dad is calling her.
   - Ex 4: Choose the correct form; play again to check. Answers: 1 seems, 2 Are you joking, 3 don’t believe, 4 are building, 5 hear, 6 ’m holding, 7 don’t sound, 8 ’s driving.
Step 3: Text completion 10 min
   - Ex 5: Giacomo’s cooking text. Answers: 1 ’s visiting, 2 ’s staying, 3 likes, 4 wants, 5 tastes, 6 ’m making, 7 ’m using, 8 looks.
   - Discuss why tastes and looks are in the present simple (state verbs).
formative: Error hunt: write four incorrect sentences on the board (e.g. She is knowing the answer). Pairs correct them and explain the rule.
closing: Reflect on learning: What new thing did you learn about present tenses today? Write one sentence about a habit and one about something you’re doing this term.

title: Lesson 3 (Part 1): Vocabulary – Personality Adjectives
materials: Student’s Book p. 17 (Ex 1–6); Audio 1.02; Practice Guide p. 71; board
outcomes:
• Understand and pronounce 12 personality adjectives and classify them as positive, negative or neutral.
• Evaluate whether qualities such as ambitious, generous and easy-going can be both positive and negative.
• Use adjective + preposition collocations (good at, keen on, interested in …) followed by a noun or -ing form.
• Complete a multiple-choice cloze, justifying each answer.
concepts:
• Personality Adjectives: unpleasant, lazy, sociable, noisy, rude, funny, clever, confident, sporty, serious, shy, calm.
• Collocations: good/brilliant at, bad/terrible at, bored/fed up with, excited about, interested in, afraid/frightened of, keen on + noun / -ing.
• Pronunciation: Weak forms of at /ət/ and of /əv/; linking: interested ‿in.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Team game: write the first letter of five personality adjectives the class probably knows (c – creative, f
   - friendly, h – honest, p – polite, s – smart). Teams write the full words; the first team with all five correct wins.
• Assessment: Diagnose the range of personality vocabulary students already have.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 17 (Ex 1–6); Audio 1.02; Practice Guide p. 71; board
Step 1: Meaning & classification 12 min
   - Ex 1: Students cover the definitions and guess, then match. Answers: 1 unpleasant, 2 lazy, 3 sociable, 4 noisy, 5 rude, 6 funny, 7 clever, 8 confident, 9 sporty, 10 serious, 11 shy, 12 calm. Drill sociable and calm.
   - Ex 2: Why are the adjectives grouped this way? (positive / negative / neutral).
   - Critical thinking: Is being ambitious / generous / easy-going always positive? Pairs give an example of when it could be negative.
Step 2: Listening – A conversation 8 min
   - Ex 3: Choose the correct words in the conversation, then Ex 4: listen to Audio 1.02 to check. Answers: 1 lazy, 2 sporty, 3 sociable, 4 calm, 5 confident, 6 rude.
   - Listen again: How does Katy feel? (annoyed) How do you know? (her words and intonation).
Step 3: Collocations & cloze 17 min
   - Explore language: elicit prepositions after good, bored, excited, interested, afraid, keen; check with the box. Practise I’m interested in science / in learning about science.
   - Ex 5 (multiple-choice cloze): Answers: 1A (interested in), 2B (act), 3C (keen on), 4A (following rules), 5B (behaviour towards), 6D (similar to). Students explain why the other options are wrong.
   - Ex 6: Pairs write yes/no questions with the collocations (Are you good at cooking?) and interview another pair.
formative: Traffic-light check: show a collocation card (e.g. keen ___); students write the preposition and hold it up. Students show green/yellow/red for how sure they are; revisit any “red” items.
closing: Students describe two family members using the new adjectives and a collocation (e.g. My brother’s quite sporty – he’s brilliant at football.). Share a few with the class.

title: Lesson 3 (Part 2): Workbook – Personality & Prepositions
materials: Workbook p. 15 (Ex 1–5); board
outcomes:
• Match personality adjectives with pictures and definitions.
• Complete short dialogues with the correct adjective.
• Choose the correct preposition after adjectives and write personalised sentences.
concepts:
• Vocabulary Review: noisy, lazy, sporty, clever, shy, calm, confident, sociable, serious.
• Collocations: at / about / with / on / in / of after adjectives.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Mime game: write calm, lazy, noisy, shy, sporty on the board. Teacher mimes one; the student who guesses first mimes the next.
• Assessment: Check instant recognition of the adjectives.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 15 (Ex 1–5); board
Step 1: Adjectives 12 min
   - Ex 1: Match words with pictures. Answers: 1 noisy, 2 lazy, 3 sporty, 4 clever, 5 shy, 6 calm.
   - Ex 2: Match sentence halves. Answers: 1D, 2E, 3F, 4A, 5C, 6B.
   - Ex 3: Complete the pairs of sentences. Answers: 1 confident, 2 lazy, 3 sociable, 4 noisy, 5 serious, 6 sporty.
Step 2: Prepositions 10 min
   - Ex 4: Choose the correct prepositions in the two texts. Answers: 1 at, 2 about, 3 at, 4 at, 5 with, 6 at, 7 on, 8 in.
Step 3: Personal writing 15 min
   - Ex 5: Students write true sentences using the given adjectives + correct preposition (with, in, about, of, at, at, with, at, at, on).
   - Pairs swap books and check each other’s prepositions before a few students read their sentences aloud.
formative: Peer check in Ex 5: partners underline each adjective + preposition and tick it if correct; the teacher checks the disputed ones.
closing: Reflect on learning: Which new adjectives did you learn today? How will you record them so you can use them again (e.g. vocabulary notebook with an example sentence)?

title: Lesson 4 (Part 1): Listening – Cities
materials: Student’s Book p. 18 (Ex 1–7); Audio 1.03, 1.04; Practice Guide p. 79; board
outcomes:
• Describe how a city makes you feel using adjectives for emotions.
• Identify whether a listening question asks for agreement, a suggestion or a feeling.
• Listen to six short conversations and choose the correct answer, recognising when speakers agree or disagree.
• Notice the position of adverbs of frequency in sentences.
concepts:
• Listening Skill: Understanding agreement and disagreement: I’d be happy with that. / Really? Not for me.
• Emotions: excited, happy, interested, pleased, relaxed, stressed.
• Grammar Preview: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb and after be: I usually stay up late. / It’s always so windy.
pre_learning:
• Actions: This or that? Give two choices (tea / coffee, watching sport / doing sport, city / village). Students turn to the left for the first choice and to the right for the second, then explain their reason to a partner. Finish with city / country to introduce the topic.
• Assessment: Check that students give a reason for their preference.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 18 (Ex 1–7); Audio 1.03, 1.04; Practice Guide p. 79; board
Step 1: Speaking – A city I know 7 min
   - Ex 1–2: Students think about a city they know (e.g. Muscat) and say how it makes them feel using the words given, then compare in pairs.
   - Model: I love Muscat because it’s full of life, but the traffic makes me feel stressed.
Step 2: Listening task 20 min
   - Ex 3: Students read questions 1–6 and decide if each asks for agreement (A), a suggestion (S) or a feeling (F). Answers: 1A, 2F, 3A, 4F, 5S, 6A.
   - Ex 4: Read the study tip; play Audio 1.03 (two friends and their dream cities). Answer: 1 B.
   - Ex 5–6: Play Audio 1.04 twice; students justify answers in pairs. Answers: 2A, 3C, 4A, 5C, 6B. Replay the relevant part for difficult questions.
Step 3: Grammar noticing 10 min
   - Ex 7: Write I hate autumn – it’s always so windy and My brother usually stays up late at weekends. Elicit the adverbs and their position. Students read the explore grammar box.
   - Students change two sentences from the box so they are true for them.
formative: After Ex 6, students show answers with fingers (1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C) for each question; for any question where many are wrong, replay the recording and ask the class to say “stop” when they hear the answer.
closing: Reflect: On a scale of 1–5, how confident do you feel about this type of multiple-choice listening task? Write one thing you will do next time to improve (e.g. underline key words before listening).

title: Lesson 4 (Part 2): Adverbs of Frequency & Time Phrases
materials: Student’s Book p. 18 (Ex 8–10); Workbook p. 16 (Ex 1–6); Audio W1.02; Grammar file SB pp. 52–53; board
outcomes:
• Put adverbs of frequency and time phrases in the correct position in a sentence.
• Write true sentences about personal habits using frequency expressions.
• Ask and answer follow-up questions about habits and routines.
• Identify key words in listening questions and answer them (extra listening practice).
concepts:
• Adverbs of Frequency: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, hardly ever, never – before the main verb / after be.
• Time Phrases: once a week, twice a year, every day, now and then, most days, from time to time – usually at the end of the sentence.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write always, often, every day, from time to time, most days, rarely, usually on the board. Students describe the weather in Oman in summer and winter using these words (e.g. It’s always hot in July.).
• Assessment: Check word order with adverbs in spontaneous sentences.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 18 (Ex 8–10); Workbook p. 16 (Ex 1–6); Audio W1.02; Grammar file SB pp. 52–53; board
Step 1: Word order 10 min
   - SB Ex 8: Order the words. Answers: 1 We can see a full moon once a month. 2 It isn’t usually dark in June. 3 I like swimming in the river now and then. 4 Tom and I go skating once a week. 5 It often rains in the middle of the day. 6 I am always tired on Thursday evenings.
   - WB Ex 4: Match the words to make time phrases: now and then, hardly ever, frequently, every day, once a month, most days.
Step 2: Controlled writing 12 min
   - WB Ex 5: Rewrite with the adverb in the right place, e.g. My parents hardly ever go to the cinema. / We rarely travel by train.
   - SB Ex 9: Students write six true sentences using the words given (e.g. I read a book most days.).
Step 3: Speaking – Find what we have in common 15 min
   - SB Ex 10: In pairs, students compare their sentences and ask follow-up questions (Where do you hang out? What do you usually do?).
   - Write follow-up question frames on the board for less confident students.
   - If time: WB Ex 1–3 (Audio W1.02) – underline key words and decide A/S/F before listening. Answers Ex 3:
1A, 2B, 3A, 4C, 5C, 6B.
formative: Class survey: each student writes one prediction about the class (e.g. Most students usually sleep before 10 p.m.), asks five classmates and reports whether it was true.
closing: WB Ex 6 (written exit ticket or homework): Write true/negative sentences such as I often take the bus. / I don’t often take the bus.

title: Lesson 5 (Part 1): Speaking – Introductions
materials: Student’s Book p. 19 (Ex 1–9); Audio 1.05, 1.06; Practice Guide p. 83; board
outcomes:
• Ask and answer questions to give personal information (name, address, free time).
• Evaluate two candidates’ answers and explain why one is better.
• Extend answers by giving reasons and examples (because, as, one reason is that, for example).
• Take part in a short interview (B1 Preliminary Speaking Part 1 style).
concepts:
• Useful Language: Reasons: because, as, one reason is (that) … / Examples: for example, such as.
• Speaking Skill: A good answer is full, descriptive and gives a reason or an example – not just one word.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write your answers to three interview questions on the board (e.g. By car. / Football. / Twice a week.). Students guess the questions (How do you get to school? …). Explain that today’s lesson is about answering such questions well.
• Assessment: Check students can form correct present simple questions.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 19 (Ex 1–9); Audio 1.05, 1.06; Practice Guide p. 83; board
Step 1: Personal information 8 min
   - Ex 1: Students answer the questions for themselves; clarify full name / surname / middle name.
   - Ex 2: Pairs ask each other questions and complete the table about their partner, then check spelling together.
Step 2: Listening & evaluating answers 14 min
   - Ex 3: Play Audio 1.05. Who gives the better answer? → Chen (fuller, more descriptive).
   - Ex 4: Using the useful language box, pairs improve Huda’s answer (where exactly she lives, why she likes it).
   - Ex 5–6: Play Audio 1.06. → Huda gives the better answer this time. Pairs plan how Chen could extend his answer with reasons and examples.
Step 3: Practice task 15 min
   - Ex 7: Students think about how to extend their answers, then interview each other.
   - Ex 8: Fact file – the teacher answers as a famous Omani person; students then do the same in pairs (they may invent details).
   - Ex 9 (Speaking extra): New pairs, new questions; monitor and note good language and common errors.
formative: Peer feedback: while one student answers, the partner ticks a simple checklist on paper – full answer ✓, reason ✓, example ✓. Partners share one strength and one suggestion.
closing: Reasons chain in groups of six: Statement on the board (e.g. Learning English is useful.). Each student adds a different reason (One reason is … / Another reason is … / Also …); a student who can’t think of one is out.

title: Lesson 5 (Part 2): Workbook – Personal Details & Interviews
materials: Workbook p. 17 (Ex 1–7); Audio W1.03, W1.04, W1.05; board
outcomes:
• Form correct questions to ask for personal details and spell names and email addresses.
• Listen and complete a membership form accurately.
• Use linking words for reasons, examples and results in an interview (because, so, for example, also).
concepts:
• Questions: What’s your middle name? / How do you spell …? / What’s your postcode? / Can you spell your email address, please?
• Linking Words: but, one reason, for example, because, so, also.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write Charles John Dickens on the board. Ask for the first name, middle name and surname, then ask a student to spell the surname. Repeat with a student’s name (if they are happy to).
• Assessment: Check the English alphabet (spelling aloud), especially vowels and similar letters (e/i, g/j).
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 17 (Ex 1–7); Audio W1.03, W1.04, W1.05; board
Step 1: Questions & form filling 14 min
   - Ex 1: Order the words to make questions (What’s your middle name? What’s your address? …).
   - Ex 2: Play Audio W1.03 and complete Emily’s form: Emily Amber Taylor, 58 Castle Street, Weybridge, KT13 8SG, emilyt@hithere.com.
   - Ex 3: Play Audio W1.04; students answer the questions for themselves in their notebooks (they may invent details).
Step 2: Question words & linking 10 min
   - Ex 4: Question words. Answers: 1 Where, 2 What, 3 What, 4 How, 5 Who, 6 Who.
   - Ex 5: Match and complete. Answers: A 2 reason, B 5 for, C 3 because, D 1 example, E 6 so, F 4 because.
Step 3: Interview 13 min
   - Ex 6: Students complete Carlos’s interview, then Ex 7: listen to Audio W1.05 to check. Answers: 1 but, 2 one reason, 3 for example, 4 because, 5 so, 6 also.
   - Pairs ask and answer the interview questions about themselves, extending each answer with a linker.
formative: Spelling dictation: each student spells their (real or invented) email address to a partner, who writes it down; they compare and correct.
closing: Reflect: On a scale of 1–5, how confident are you with the introductions task? Write one way to practise further (e.g. record yourself answering at home).

title: Lesson 6 (Part 1): Writing – An Email (Personal Profile)
materials: Student’s Book pp. 20–21 (Ex 1–9); Practice Guide p. 73; board
outcomes:
• Read a model email and match each paragraph with the content points in the task.
• Use quite and very to modify adjectives correctly (quite an exciting city / a very old part).
• Join ideas with and, but, so, because and or.
• Plan and write an email of about 100 words that covers all four content points.
concepts:
• Writing Skill: Modifying adjectives: very + adjective; quite + adjective; quite a/an + adjective + noun / a very + adjective + noun.
• Linkers: and (add), but (contrast), so (result), because (reason), or (alternative).
• Exam Tip: Write about every content point in the task (Content criterion).
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write: I really enjoy watching … because … / Something I hate watching is … because … . Students complete both sentences and compare in pairs. Find out what is popular in the class and why.
• Assessment: Check that students can give clear reasons in writing and speaking.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 20–21 (Ex 1–9); Practice Guide p. 73; board
Step 1: Speaking & reading the model 12 min
   - Ex 1: In pairs, students talk about something they love, are interested in, are keen on and can’t stand.
   - Ex 2: Read the TV advert and Rahaf’s notes A–D, then match the email paragraphs: 1A, 2B, 3C, 4D.
   - Critical thinking: advantages and disadvantages of appearing on a reality TV show – would you apply? Why / why not?
Step 2: Language focus 12 min
   - Ex 3: Find quite and very in the email; read the explore language box. Practise: I’m a very hard-working student. / I’m quite a hard-working student.
   - Ex 4: Complete Filip’s notes. Answers: 1 quite an exciting, 2 a very old, 3 very keen on, 4 quite interested, 5 very funny.
   - Ex 5: Join the sentences using and, because, but, or, so (e.g. I’m not very keen on maths, so I prefer subjects like art and P.E.). Plan and write 13 min
STEP 3
   - Ex 6–7: Students make notes for the four points (where I live, my personality, what I enjoy, why choose me) and check the study tip.
   - Ex 8: Students start writing their 100-word email in class and finish it for homework (lower-ability students may write about 70 words).
   - Ex 9 (Improve it): Next lesson, partners give feedback using I liked the way you … / Maybe next time you could …
formative: Before writing, students swap their plans and check that all four content points are covered; the partner puts a tick next to each point. The teacher checks a sample of plans.
closing: Role-play: Group A are the TV production team and prepare two interview questions; Group B are applicants. Pairs role-play a one-minute interview and the team decides who to accept, giving a reason.

title: Lesson 6 (Part 2): Workbook – School Council Email
materials: Workbook p. 18 (Ex 1–6); students’ emails from the previous lesson; board
outcomes:
• Give and receive peer feedback on the emails written for homework.
• Classify sentences as personality, hobbies or likes/dislikes, and use quite/very correctly.
• Analyse a model email for a school council position and write their own application email.
concepts:
• Task Analysis: An email answering four points: personality, the best thing about you, what you are good at, why the class should choose you.
• Review: Adjective + preposition (at, with, on, in); quite and very.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Improve it (SB Ex 9): partners read each other’s homework emails and give one positive comment and one suggestion using the sentence frames on the board. Then ask: What is a school council? Who would make a good class representative?
• Assessment: Listen to the quality of the feedback; praise specific, helpful comments.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 18 (Ex 1–6); students’ emails from the previous lesson; board
Step 1: Language review 12 min
   - Ex 1: Personality (P), likes/dislikes (LD) or hobby (H)? Answers: 1P, 2LD, 3H, 4LD, 5LD, 6P, 7H.
   - Ex 2: Group adjectives by preposition – at: brilliant, good, terrible; with: bored, fed up; on: keen; in:
interested.
   - Ex 3: quite/very. Answers: 1 quite keen, 2 quite a serious, 3 very confident, 4 very scared, 5 quite interested, 6 very shy.
Step 2: Reading the model 8 min
   - Ex 4: Read the school council advert. What should you write? (an email) How many points? (four).
   - Ex 5: Read Dana’s email and answer the questions (1 yes, 2 yes, 3 yes – serious, friendly, good at …, 4 quite and very).
Step 3: Writing 17 min
   - Ex 6: Students plan, then write their own email to become class representative.
   - Students check their email against the Ex 5 questions before handing it in.
formative: Self-check list on the board: four points covered? quite/very used? at least two linkers? adjective + preposition used correctly? Students tick each item before submitting; the teacher marks a sample.
closing: Ask: Which parts of Unit 1 did you enjoy most and why? Announce that the next lesson reviews the whole unit.

title: Lesson 7: Switch On – Learning is fun!
materials: Student’s Book p. 22 (Ex 1–7); Unit 1 video (or the teacher reads the video script aloud if no projector is available); paper for the project; board
outcomes:
• Discuss where and how people learn new skills at different ages.
• Understand the main idea and key details of a short programme about lifelong learning.
• Use verb + noun collocations (arrange flowers, repair a car, take a class, join a class).
• Work in a group to prepare and present an information sheet about an evening class.
concepts:
• Main Idea: People of all ages can learn, anywhere and at any time; learning builds confidence and new friendships.
• Collocations: arrange flowers, repair a car, take an evening class, join a class, make friends, give confidence.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Ex 1–2 (Preview): Pairs discuss: Where do you usually learn how to do things? Is learning only for young people? Pairs join into groups of four and compare; groups justify any disagreements.
• Assessment: Check students can express and justify an opinion politely.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 22 (Ex 1–7); Unit 1 video (or the teacher reads the video script aloud if no projector is available); paper for the project; board
Step 1: View for gist 8 min
   - Ex 3: Play the video (or read the script aloud with three students reading the parts). Question: What is the main message? → You can learn to do things at any age and anywhere.
Step 2: View for detail & collocations 12 min
   - Ex 4: Complete the summary; replay/re-read once. Answers: 1 life, 2 evening, 3 clothes, 4 bike, 5 oil, 6 confident, 7 people, 8 from home, 9 video, 10 time.
   - Ex 5: Complete the sentences with arrange, give, join, make, repair, take. Answers: 1 arrange, 2 repair, 3 take, 4 joined, 5 made, gave.
Step 3: Discussion & project 17 min
   - Ex 6: Groups discuss the questions (How are evening classes different from school? How can practical skills help?).
   - Ex 7 (Project): In small groups, students choose an evening class (e.g. car repair, cooking, a new language) and prepare an information sheet on paper: what you learn, when, who it is for, why join.
   - Groups display their sheets; other groups ask one question each. Class vote for the most interesting class.
formative: During the project, the teacher visits each group with two questions: Why would someone join this class? What would they learn? Every group member must answer at least one question.
closing: Each student completes the sentence: One new skill I would like to learn is … because … , and shares it with a partner.

title: Lesson 8 (Part 1): Unit Check – Review
materials: Student’s Book pp. 23–24 (Wordlist, Practice Ex 1–4, Review Ex 1–6); Audio 1.07, 1.08; Grammar file SB pp. 50–53; board
outcomes:
• Review and consolidate present simple vs present continuous and adverbs of frequency.
• Recall personality adjectives and adjective + preposition collocations from the unit.
• Identify correct sentences by listening and explain the grammar reason.

concepts:
• Grammar: Present simple / present continuous; state verbs; adverbs of frequency and time phrases.
• Vocabulary: Personality adjectives; adjective + preposition collocations; wordlist p. 23.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Spelling quiz from the wordlist: in pairs, students test each other on six words from the unit (e.g. sociable, confident, background, stadium). Then talk about three things they do every week and one thing they are doing now.
• Assessment: Identify which words and structures are still weak.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 23–24 (Wordlist, Practice Ex 1–4, Review Ex 1–6); Audio 1.07, 1.08; Grammar file SB pp. 50–53; board
Step 1: Grammar review 14 min
   - Review Ex 1: Choose the correct words. Answers: 1 is thinking, 2 doesn’t see, 3 Do you understand, 4 am looking, 5 don’t enjoy, 6 It’s raining, 7 Is she playing, 8 am learning, 9 is getting ready, 10 I don’t know.
   - Review Ex 2: Order the sentences (e.g. Fatima and Raya play volleyball now and then. / Osama is never late for school.).
Step 2: Vocabulary & listening 12 min
   - Practice Ex 3: Complete with adjective + preposition, then listen to Audio 1.07. Answers: 1 excited about, 2 keen on, 3 terrible at, 4 bad at, 5 brilliant at, 6 keen on.

Step 3: Text completion & writing 11 min
   - Review Ex 5: Complete the text. Answers: 1 that/which, 2 in, 3 are, 4 on, 5 going, 6 the.

title: Lesson 8 (Part 2): Workbook – Unit 1 Revision

pre_learning:
• Actions: Teacher models: Every week, I play football on Saturdays and visit my grandparents. Today, I’m helping you revise! Students say three things they do every week and one thing they are doing now.
• Assessment: Quick oral check of present tense accuracy.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 19 (Ex 1–6); board
Reading & grammar 14 min
STEP 1
   - Ex 1: Complete the blog post about Lew. Answers: 1 speak, 2 ’m speaking, 3 is staying, 4 comes, 5 doesn’t know, 6 doesn’t understand, 7 is improving, 8 isn’t getting.

   - Ex 4: Complete with personality adjectives. Answers: 1 rude, 2 sociable, 3 sporty, 4 shy, 5 clever, 6 funny, 7 lazy, 8 noisy, 9 serious, 10 confident.

   - Ex 5 (multiple choice): 1D different from, 2C bad at, 3A interested in, 4C hang out with, 5B join in, 6C less … than.
   - Ex 6 (open cloze): 1 on, 2 once, 3 perform, 4 from, 5 ’m, 6 about.

title: Lesson 1 (Part 1): Reading – The importance of languages
materials: Student’s Book pp. 25–27 (Opener, Ex 1–11); Practice Guide pp. 63, 67; board
outcomes:
• Discuss different ways people communicate and explain the meaning of the quote “It’s good to talk”.
• Understand the main message of short texts (a notice and a message) and choose the option that matches all the information.
• Read a long article about minority languages in Canada and answer detailed and whole-text multiple-choice questions.
• Take part in a structured debate for and against protecting languages that are dying out.
concepts:
• Reading Skill: Understanding the main point – options use synonyms, not the same words as the text; the last question tests the whole text.
• Vocabulary: slightly, occurred, realised, allowed, discovered, alive, at risk, original, official language, community, culture.
• Value: Languages carry the stories, traditions and memories of a community – Arabic is part of our identity.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Category race: write a country (S), a language (C), a currency (R), a capital city (A). Teams have three minutes to write one answer for each starting with that letter (e.g. Sudan, Chinese, Rial, Amman). Two points for a unique answer, one point for a shared one.
• Assessment: Activate general knowledge about languages and countries; check spelling.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 25–27 (Opener, Ex 1–11); Practice Guide pp. 63, 67; board
Step 1: Language quiz & discussion 8 min
   - Write Zulu, Inuktitut, Gaelic, Maori, Welsh on the board – what are they? (languages). Ex 1: pairs decide if the quiz statements are true or false; Ex 2: check on p. 58 – they are all true.
   - Ex 3: Pairs discuss the questions about the languages they speak and would like to learn.
Step 2: Short texts – multiple choice 10 min
   - Ex 4: Where would you see each text? (top: a school notice; bottom: a phone message). Check low grades.
   - Ex 5: Choose the option that matches all the information. Answers: 1 C (Contact your teacher if you are interested), 2 B (money for the trip is due on Friday). Students explain why the other options are wrong. Long text, vocabulary & debate 19 min
STEP 3
   - Ex 6: Predict from the heading, then read: which languages are mentioned? (English, French, Cree, Ojibwe, Inuktitut).
   - Ex 7–8: Read the study tip; underline key words in the questions. Answers: 1B, 2D, 3A, 4D, 5A. Students quote the sentence that proves each answer.
   - Ex 9: Find words with these meanings. Answers: 1 slightly, 2 occurred, 3 realised, 4 allowed me, 5 discovered, 6 alive, 7 at risk, 8 original.
   - Ex 10 (Sum up) & Ex 11 (Speak): Groups split into for/against: Should we spend money protecting languages that are dying out? Prompts: culture, money, time, technology.
formative: Sum up check: fast finishers write a two-line summary beginning “The writer believes that … because …”; the teacher reads two aloud and the class judges whether they capture the main idea.
closing: Reflect on learning: What was the most interesting thing you learnt about languages today? Each group gives one reason why Arabic is important to protect and develop.

title: Lesson 1 (Part 2): Workbook – Learning Wolof
materials: Workbook pp. 20–21 (Ex 1–6); board
outcomes:

• Read a blog about learning a language and answer multiple-choice questions, including one about the writer’s overall attitude.

• Vocabulary Review: alive, original, discovered, slightly, occurred, realised, allowed, at risk.
• Reading Skill: Identifying the writer’s overall attitude (positive / negative).
pre_learning:
• Actions: In four minutes, groups list as many languages as they can. Then each student says which language they would like to learn and why.
• Assessment: Check students can give a reason for their choice.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook pp. 20–21 (Ex 1–6); board
Step 1: Vocabulary 10 min
   - Ex 1: Complete the sentences. Answers: 1 alive, 2 original, 3 discovered, 4 slightly, 5 occurred, 6 realised, 7 allowed, 8 risk.
   - Ex 2: Match with the sentences in Ex 1. Answers: 1G, 2C, 3H, 4F, 5B, 6E, 7D, 8A.
Step 2: Short texts 8 min
   - Ex 3: Answers: 1 A (Fatma asks her dad to take her notes to reception), 2 B (all students can go but need permission), 3 C (the buyer will pay more than 150 for a guitar in excellent condition).
Step 3: Long text – Léa’s blog 19 min
   - Ex 4: Read quickly – is Léa’s experience positive or negative? (positive).
   - Ex 5: Answers: 1D, 2C, 3C, 4B, 5A. Students underline the evidence in the blog.
   - Ex 6: Answers: 1A, 2B, 3A, 4B, 5A, 6A.

title: Lesson 2 (Part 1): Grammar – Past Simple & Past Continuous
materials: Student’s Book p. 28 (Ex 1–7); Audio 2.01; Grammar file SB pp. 54–55; board
outcomes:
• Use the past continuous for an action in progress and the past simple for a completed or interrupting action.
• Recognise that state verbs (understand, want, hear, know) are not used in the past continuous.
• Listen to teenagers describing past moments and complete sentences with the correct past forms.
• Talk about what they were doing at specific times in the past.
concepts:
• Past Continuous: was/were + -ing: While I was chatting with some local teenagers, …
• Past Simple: Completed or interrupting actions: … I realised that my French skills were useful.
• Spelling: come → coming, travel → travelling, stop → stopping, lie → lying.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Write: While I was chatting with some local teenagers, I realised that my French skills were useful. Underline the verbs and ask which tenses they are and why each is used.
• Assessment: Check whether students can name and explain the two tenses.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 28 (Ex 1–7); Audio 2.01; Grammar file SB pp. 54–55; board
Step 1: Presenting the grammar 10 min
   - Ex 1: When did the writer realise French was useful? (on a family trip in France, while chatting to teenagers).
   - Ex 2: Read explore grammar 1 and answer: regular past = -ed; irregular examples came, had, saw, went; past continuous = was/were + -ing.
Step 2: Listening 12 min
   - Ex 3: Play Audio 2.01 – which questions do the speakers answer? (A and B).
   - Ex 4: Complete the sentences, then listen again to check. Answers: 1 was walking, 2 was cleaning / got, 3 was playing / had, 4 was practising / called, 5 was / heard, 6 was doing / rang.
Step 3: State verbs, text & speaking 15 min
   - Ex 5: Write know, like, hate, hear – why can’t we say I was knowing? Read explore grammar 2 (answer:
didn’t understand).
   - Ex 6: Article about phone calls. Answers: 1 didn’t understand, 2 didn’t want, 3 heard, 4 was listening, 5 realised, 6 were working, 7 chatted, 8 changed, 9 visited, 10 understood, 11 called, 12 loved.
   - Ex 7: Pairs discuss the questions using both tenses.
formative: Two truths game: each student writes one true and one false sentence about last week using both tenses; the partner asks questions and guesses which is true. The teacher monitors for tense accuracy.
closing: Pairs tell each other what they were doing yesterday at 6 a.m., 7.30 a.m., 5 p.m. and 10 p.m. and find one similarity.

title: Lesson 2 (Part 2): Workbook – Past Tenses Practice
materials: Workbook p. 22 (Ex 1–6); Audio W2.01; board
outcomes:

• Past Forms: carry – carried, come – came, hear – heard, stop – stopped, try – tried, win – won.

• Actions: Write 4 a.m., 7 a.m., 7.30 a.m., 8.30 a.m. on the board. Model what you were doing at each time this morning; students do the same in pairs.
• Assessment: Check was/were + -ing in quick spoken answers.

Materials: Workbook p. 22 (Ex 1–6); Audio W2.01; board
Past simple forms 6 min
STEP 1
   - Ex 1: Complete the table: carried, came, had, heard, lived, stopped, tried, won. Drill /t/, /d/, /ɪd/ endings.
Step 2: Listening – 8 o’clock last night 12 min
   - Ex 2: Complete the sentences, then Ex 3: listen to Audio W2.01 to check. Answers: 1 was messaging, 2 were learning / weren’t doing, 3 were having / weren’t arguing, 4 was raining / was standing, 5 was telling / wasn’t listening, 6 were playing / wasn’t enjoying, 7 was trying / was finding, 8 was sleeping / was watching.

   - Ex 5: Answers: 1 was living / took, 2 were they talking / came, 3 didn’t speak / were staying, 4 arrived / were eating, 5 didn’t use / were travelling, 6 was speaking / wasn’t.
   - Ex 6: Conversation. Answers: 1 Did you take, 2 didn’t need, 3 had, 4 was studying, 5 used, 6 was sightseeing, 7 became, 8 didn’t have to, 9 didn’t get, 10 was walking. Pairs read it aloud.

title: Lesson 3 (Part 1): Vocabulary – Language & Communication
materials: Student’s Book p. 29 (Ex 1–5); Audio 2.02; Practice Guide p. 71; board
outcomes:
• Understand and use communication verbs (repeat, say, translate, mean, speak, pronounce, understand, explain).
• Use verb + preposition collocations correctly (listen to, talk to/about, explain something to someone).
• Distinguish commonly confused pairs: say/tell, talk/speak, listen/hear.
• Complete a multiple-choice cloze and justify answers.
concepts:
• Verbs: repeat, say, translate, mean, speak, pronounce, understand, explain, tell, talk, listen, hear.
• Collocations: listen to, talk to/about, speak to (about), explain something to someone – not explain me / said him.
• Confusing Pairs: tell a story / say the alphabet / speak a language / listen to / hear a noise.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Closed books. Write Communication on the board. Pairs have two minutes to list verbs related to communication (speak, understand …). Collect them on the board.
• Assessment: Check existing vocabulary range.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 29 (Ex 1–5); Audio 2.02; Practice Guide p. 71; board
Step 1: Communication verbs 12 min
   - Ex 1: Discuss: How can you communicate without a shared language? (gestures, pictures, translation apps).
   - Ex 2: Complete the sentences, then listen to Audio 2.02. Answers: 1 repeat, 2 say, 3 translate, 4 means, 5 speak, 6 pronounce, 7 understand / explain.
Step 2: Prepositions & confusing pairs 12 min
   - Explore language: which prepositions follow listen, talk, speak, explain? Board check: I said him / to him … ✗ → I told him …
   - Ex 3: Answers: A 1 Tell, 2 tell, 3 talk; B 4 Say, 5 speak, 6 speak; C 7 listen, 8 Listen, 9 hear. Students explain each choice.
Step 3: Multiple-choice cloze & speaking 13 min
   - Ex 4: Answers: 1D translate, 2A spoke, 3B explain, 4C repeat, 5B pronounce, 6A understand.
   - Ex 5: Small groups discuss the questions; the teacher notes errors with the target verbs.

concepts: • Review: will / be going to / present continuous / present simple for the future.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Quick questions: What time does today’s lesson start? (It starts at …) Sara doesn’t have a pen – who will lend her one? (I will.) I have tickets to Athens – where am I going? (You’re going to Greece.)
• Assessment: Check instant choice of future forms.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 30 (Ex 1–6); Audio W3.01; board
Step 1: Word order & choosing forms 13 min
   - Ex 1: e.g. Are you going to book your ticket? / The play starts at eight o’clock. / We’re meeting Lucas this evening.
   - Ex 2: Answers: 1 ’ll turn up, 2 ’ll put, 3 ’s meeting, 4 won’t need, 5 are you going, 6 ’m not doing, 7 ’ll explain, 8 ’re going. Which are offers/decisions (1, 2, 7), predictions (4) and arrangements (3, 5, 6, 8)?
Step 2: Listening – Buying a gift 12 min
   - Ex 3: Complete the conversation, then Ex 4: listen to Audio W3.01. Answers: 1 ’m going to buy, 2 ’ll come, 3 isn’t going to take, 4 ’re going to have, 5 ’ll probably be, 6 won’t buy, 7 ’m going.
Step 3: Conversation & writing 12 min
   - Ex 5: Answers: 1 are you doing, 2 ’m going to go, 3 starts, 4 ’ll finish, 5 ’ll probably take, 6 ’s picking, 7 ’s going to be, 8 ’ll be.
   - Ex 6: Students plan and start a paragraph about their plans for the next school holiday (finish for homework).
formative: Students underline each future form in their Ex 6 paragraph and label it (A = arrangement, I = intention, P = prediction); partners check the labels.
closing: Reflect: Which future form do you find most difficult? Why? Ask: Which technology in your home is the most useful? (preparing for the next lesson).

title: Lesson 3 (Part 1): Vocabulary – Technology in the home & Phrasal Verbs
materials: Student’s Book p. 41 (Ex 1–7); Practice Guide p. 71; board
outcomes:
• Name and correctly stress words for household appliances.
• Understand and use phrasal verbs for technology (switch on/off, turn up/down, plug in, set up, go off, come on).
• Know which phrasal verbs are separable and where to put object pronouns.
• Complete a multiple-choice cloze about smart homes.
concepts:
• Appliances: kettle, microwave, TV, fridge-freezer, washing machine, dishwasher, coffee maker, speaker, air conditioning.
• Phrasal Verbs: switch on/off, turn up/down, plug in, set up (separable); go off, come on (inseparable).
• Grammar Note: Take your shoes off / Take off your shoes ✓ – take them off ✓ – take off them ✗.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Teams have two minutes to list technology found in the home. The team with the longest correct list reads it aloud; the class checks.
• Assessment: Check existing vocabulary and spelling.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 41 (Ex 1–7); Practice Guide p. 71; board
Step 1: Appliances 8 min
   - Ex 1: Label the photos: A kettle, B microwave, C TV, D fridge-freezer, E washing machine, F dishwasher, G coffee maker, H speaker, I air conditioning. Mark the stress.
   - Ex 2: Pairs agree on the three most useful appliances and justify.
Step 2: Phrasal verbs 14 min
   - Ex 3: Match the phrasal verbs with the meanings. Answers: 1D, 2H, 3B, 4A, 5F, 6E, 7C, 8G.
   - Ex 4: Read explore language – all are separable except go off and come on.
   - Board check: Don’t forget your shoes – take off them ✗ → take them off ✓.
   - Ex 5: Pairs say which sentences are true for them (e.g. I always switch off the lights – it saves electricity).
Step 3: Cloze & speaking 15 min
   - Ex 6: Answers: 1B, 2B, 3C, 4A (connect to), 5D, 6C (reminds). Students explain why the other options are wrong.
   - Ex 7: Pairs think of a problem at home and invent a smart device to solve it; present it to the class.
formative: Drawing game: a student draws a clue on the board (e.g. plug and socket); the class guesses the phrasal verb and uses it in a sentence with a pronoun in the correct position.
closing: Discuss: How smart is your home? What will homes be like in thirty years? Each student makes one prediction using will.

title: Lesson 3 (Part 2): Workbook – When the power went off
materials: Workbook p. 31 (Ex 1–7); Audio W3.02; board
outcomes:
• Form compound nouns for appliances and use them in context.
• Use technology phrasal verbs correctly in sentences.
• Listen to a conversation about a power cut and complete a summary.
concepts:
• Vocabulary: microwave, coffee maker, fridge-freezer, TV, air conditioning, kettle, washing machine, dishwasher.
• Phrasal Verbs: switch off, turn down, switch on, set up, plug in, turn up, come on, go off.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Students name as many kitchen technologies as they can; collect them on the board and hold a class vote on the most important one.
• Assessment: Recall of last lesson’s vocabulary.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 31 (Ex 1–7); Audio W3.02; board
Step 1: Compound nouns 10 min
   - Ex 1: Match the halves: 1E, 2C, 3A, 4F, 5D, 6B (dishwasher and microwave are one word).
   - Ex 2: 1 microwave, 2 coffee maker, 3 fridge-freezer, 4 TV, 5 air conditioning, 6 kettle, 7 washing machine, 8 dishwasher.
Step 2: Phrasal verbs 8 min
   - Ex 3: 1 switch off, 2 turn down, 3 switch on, 4 set up, 5 plug in, 6 turn up, 7 come on, 8 goes off.
Step 3: Listening & cloze 19 min
   - Ex 4: Play Audio W3.02 – what happened? (The power went off for two days.)
   - Ex 5: Complete and listen again: 1 went off, 2 microwave, 3 fridge-freezer, 4 dishwasher, 5 plug in, 6 came on.
   - Ex 6: Blog cloze: 1A, 2C, 3C, 4B, 5C, 6D.
   - Ex 7: Students write a short paragraph: What would you do if the power went off for two days?
formative: Pairs test each other: one says the meaning (make the music louder), the other says the phrasal verb and a sentence (turn it up).
closing: Reflect: Which new phrasal verbs did you learn today? How will you record them (e.g. with a picture and an example sentence)?

title: Lesson 4 (Part 1): Listening – Discussing technology
materials: Student’s Book p. 42 (Ex 1–7); Audio 3.02; Practice Guide p. 77; Grammar file SB pp. 56–57; board
outcomes:
• Predict the topic and key words of a conversation from three pictures.
• Listen to seven short conversations and choose the correct picture, ignoring distractors.
• Give advice and suggestions using should, ought to, could, Why don’t you …?, How about + -ing?, Shall I/we …?
• Role-play asking for and giving advice about a technology problem.
concepts:
• Listening Skill: Identifying differences – all three pictures are mentioned, but only one answers the question.
• Advice & Suggestions: You should / shouldn’t …, You ought to …, You could …, Why don’t you …?, Shall we …?, How about + noun/-ing?
pre_learning:
• Actions: In pairs, students talk about their favourite piece of technology: what it is, what they use it for and why they like it.
• Assessment: Check fluency and topic vocabulary.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 42 (Ex 1–7); Audio 3.02; Practice Guide p. 77; Grammar file SB pp. 56–57; board
Step 1: Prediction 8 min
   - Ex 1: Look at question 1 (tablet, smartphone, smartwatch) – which do you have? Quick class survey.
   - Ex 2: Read the study tip; predict the topic and key words for question 1 (buying something new: tablet, phone, smartwatch).
Step 2: Multiple choice – pictures 17 min
   - Ex 3: Name each picture first (printer, earbuds, fitness app, sandwich toaster, batteries, diving …). Play Audio 3.02.
   - Ex 4: Play again; compare and justify. Answers: 1A, 2A, 3B, 4B, 5A, 6C, 7C. Replay disputed items and identify the distractors.
Step 3: Advice language & role-play 12 min
   - Ex 5: Which conversations included advice or suggestions? (1, 2, 4, 5, 6). Read explore grammar – which phrase is different? (How about + noun/-ing; the rest + bare infinitive).
   - Ex 6: Answers: 1 should/shall, 2 shouldn’t, 3 could, 4 ought, 5 don’t, 6 Shall/How about/Why don’t.
   - Ex 7: A/B role-play – one student has a technology problem, the other gives advice.
formative: Advice chain: the teacher gives a problem (My phone battery dies quickly.). Students give advice around the class, each using a different structure; others correct the verb form if needed.
closing: Mingle: students share a real or invented problem with three classmates and report the best advice they received.

title: Lesson 4 (Part 2): Workbook – Listening & Advice
materials: Workbook p. 32 (Ex 1–6); Audio W3.03, W3.04; board
outcomes:
• Identify the purpose of listening questions and predict words that will be heard.
• Listen to seven conversations and choose the correct answers.
• Complete a conversation with advice and suggestion phrases and write a short reply giving advice.
concepts: • Advice Phrases: Why don’t …?, should, could, Shall …?, ought to, How about getting …?
pre_learning:
• Actions: Students name technologies they use at home or at school; class vote on the most important one.
• Assessment: Vocabulary recall.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 32 (Ex 1–6); Audio W3.03, W3.04; board
Step 1: Before listening 10 min
   - Ex 1: Match the questions with their purposes: A6, B5, C1, D2, E4, F3, G7.
   - Ex 2: Predict which words will be heard in each conversation (e.g. dishwasher – 1, comedy – 3, quarter to nine – 4).
Step 2: Listening 15 min
   - Ex 3: Play Audio W3.03 twice. Answers: 1C, 2A, 3B, 4B, 5A, 6A, 7C. Students quote the words that gave each answer.
Step 3: Advice language 12 min
   - Ex 4: Complete the conversation, then Ex 5: listen to Audio W3.04. Answers: 1 Why, 2 should, 3 could, 4 Shall, 5 ought, 6 getting.
   - Ex 6: Students write a reply giving advice to a friend with a problem.
formative: Students compare their predictions in Ex 2 with what they actually heard and tick the correct ones; the class discusses how prediction helps.
closing: Reflect: On a scale of 1–5, how confident do you feel about multiple-choice picture tasks? What will you do before listening next time?

title: Lesson 5 (Part 1): Speaking – Collaborative task & discussion
materials: Student’s Book pp. 43, 59, 61 (Ex 1–8); Audio 3.03; Practice Guide pp. 87, 89; board
outcomes:
• Give and ask for opinions, and agree or disagree politely.
• Listen to two candidates and identify which AI assistant they choose and why.
• Discuss options with a partner and try to reach a decision (B1 Preliminary Speaking Part 3 style).
• Answer follow-up discussion questions about technology with reasons.
concepts:
• Giving Opinions: In my opinion, In my view, For me, I think / don’t think, I’d say …
• Asking: What’s your view on …? What do you think?
• Agreeing / Disagreeing: That’s a good point. / You’re right. / I disagree. / That’s true, but … / I’m not sure.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Students close their eyes and imagine a robot: What does it look like? What does it do? Pairs describe their robots and compare. Ex 1: discuss what a robot could do for you.
• Assessment: Check descriptive language and opinions.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 43, 59, 61 (Ex 1–8); Audio 3.03; Practice Guide pp. 87, 89; board
Step 1: Listening to a model 10 min
   - Ex 2: Play Audio 3.03 – which AI assistants do they discuss? (household, doctor, clothes) Which do they choose? (clothes assistant – it helps you feel confident).
   - Ex 3: Complete the extracts. Answers: 1 opinion, true; 2 view, disagree; 3 on, sure; 4 say, good; 5 For, right.
Step 2: Useful language 7 min
   - Ex 4: Group the phrases into giving opinions / asking for opinions / agreeing / disagreeing. Note: we often disagree politely with That’s true, but …
   - Ex 5: Read the study tip; each student chooses three phrases they don’t usually use.
Step 3: Practice task & discussion 20 min
   - Ex 6: Pairs discuss which AI assistant would be most useful (teacher, shopping, decorating …) and try to agree, using their chosen phrases.
   - Ex 7: Pairs answer the discussion questions with reasons.
   - Ex 8 (Speaking extra): Half the class argues the advantages, half the disadvantages of each situation; finish with a class vote.
formative: After Ex 6, pairs self-assess: Did we try to agree? Did we listen and respond to each other? Did we use our three phrases? Repeat the task with a new partner if time allows.
closing: Groups design a robot: what it does, what it looks like and why it is useful, and present it in one minute.

title: Lesson 5 (Part 2): Workbook – Opinions & Agreement
materials: Workbook p. 33 (Ex 1–6); Audio W3.05, W3.06; board
outcomes:
• Describe and compare pictures of people watching films in different places.
• Listen to a discussion and identify points of agreement.
• Classify and use phrases for giving opinions, agreeing and disagreeing in a conversation.
concepts: • Phrases: I think, For me, In my view / That’s true, That’s a good point, You’re right / I’m not sure, I don’t agree.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Students recall what they said about AI assistants last lesson – what was good and what was bad?
• Assessment: Use of opinion phrases.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 33 (Ex 1–6); Audio W3.05, W3.06; board
Step 1: Pictures 7 min
   - Ex 1: Describe pictures A–E (tablet, home cinema, alone, laptop, cinema). What do they have in common? (people watching films).
Step 2: Listening 15 min
   - Ex 2: Play Audio W3.05 and choose the options: 1 think, 2 true, 3 point, 4 right, 5 sure, 6 For, 7 agree, 8 view.
   - Ex 3: Which options do the speakers agree on? (A, B, E).
Step 3: Language practice 15 min
   - Ex 4: Classify: giving opinions – I think, For me, In my view; agreeing – That’s true, that’s a good point, You’re right; disagreeing – I’m not sure, I don’t agree.
   - Ex 5: 1 I think, 2 I don’t agree, 3 that’s true / you’re right, 4 I’m not sure, 5 For me / In my view, 6 that’s true. Pairs read it aloud.
   - Ex 6: Play Audio W3.06 – students respond to four opinion questions using the phrases.
formative: Phrase tally: while students answer Ex 6 in pairs, the partner counts how many different phrases are used; aim for at least four.
closing: Reflect: How confident are you with the collaborative task (1–5)? Ask: Have you ever helped someone use technology? (preparing for the writing lesson).

title: Lesson 6 (Part 1): Writing – An Email giving advice
materials: Student’s Book pp. 44–45 (Ex 1–12); Practice Guide p. 73; board
outcomes:
• Read a notice and an email and identify all the points the reply must include.
• Analyse a model email for paragraphing and informal style.
• Use a range of phrases to give advice and make suggestions.
• Plan and write an informal email of about 100 words answering four prompts.
concepts:
• Writing Skill: Giving advice and suggestions: I think you ought to … / You should … / Why don’t you …? / You could … / How about …?
• Organisation: Paragraph 1 – respond to the news; Paragraph 2 – advice; Paragraph 3 – your own plan; friendly ending.
• Style: Informal: Hi …, contractions, friendly phrases.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Pairs discuss: Who do you go to when you need help with technology? Do you ever help others? Who?
• Assessment: Check students can talk about helping others with reasons.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 44–45 (Ex 1–12); Practice Guide p. 73; board
Step 1: Reading the task & model 12 min
   - Ex 1: Predict what Teen Tech Help Month is; read the notice and discuss the questions.
   - Ex 2–3: Why is Arwa writing? What four things must Jood include? Does she include them all? (yes).
   - Ex 4: Analyse Jood’s email – three paragraphs; informal style (Hi, contractions).
Step 2: Advice language 10 min
   - Ex 5: Identify the function of the highlighted phrases: expressing concern, giving advice, making suggestions, giving a reason.
   - Ex 6: Complete the prompts with suggestions for Jood (You should help older people use their phones. / How about helping people set up websites?).
Step 3: Plan and write 15 min
   - Ex 7–8: Read Khalid’s email, answer the questions and plan the reply in paragraphs.
   - Ex 9: Write the email (about 100 words) – start in class, finish for homework.
   - Ex 10–12 (Improve it): self-check questions, rewrite weak parts, read twice (meaning, then accuracy).
formative: Plan swap: partners check that the plan covers all four prompts and includes at least two different advice phrases before writing begins.
closing: Groups predict how technology will change transport, healthcare, education and communication, and choose one prediction they are sure will come true.

title: Lesson 6 (Part 2): Workbook – Advice Email
materials: Workbook p. 34 (Ex 1–6); students’ homework emails; board
outcomes:
• Analyse a writing task and a model email (true/false questions).
• Match notes with ideas and complete advice phrases.
• Plan and write an advice email using a range of phrases.
concepts: • Advice Phrases: Why don’t you …? / You ought to … / Shall we …? / You should … / You could …
pre_learning:
• Actions: A few students read the emails they wrote for homework; the class identifies the advice phrases used and gives positive feedback.
• Assessment: Range of advice language in students’ writing.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook p. 34 (Ex 1–6); students’ homework emails; board
Step 1: Task analysis 10 min
   - Ex 1: True or false? 1 F (it’s an email), 2 T, 3 F (to ask for advice), 4 T, 5 F (around 100 words).
   - Ex 2: Match ideas with the notes: A3, B2, C4, D1, E2, F2, G4.
Step 2: Advice language 10 min
   - Ex 3: Match the halves: 1G, 2A, 3D, 4B, 5C, 6E, 7F.
   - Ex 4: Complete Sara’s email: 1 you, 2 to, 3 Shall, 4 should.
   - Ex 5: Does Sara include all four points in clear paragraphs? (yes).
Step 3: Writing 17 min
   - Ex 6: Students plan, then write their own email using as many advice phrases as possible.
formative: Checklist before handing in: four points covered, three paragraphs, at least three different advice phrases, informal opening and ending. Students tick each item.
closing: Ask: Would you like to help in a primary school, hospital or charity one day? Who would you help and why?

title: Lesson 7: Switch On – Technology helps everyone
materials: Student’s Book p. 46 (Ex 1–8); Unit 3 video (or the teacher reads the video script aloud if no projector is available); paper for the project; board
outcomes:
• Discuss how technology helps people stay healthy and who has access to it.
• Understand key information about telemedicine, wearable devices, cochlear implants, 3D printing, digital scanners, AI and drones.
• Complete sentences with key vocabulary from the programme.
• Design and present a new health technology in a group.
concepts:
• Vocabulary: telemedicine, wearable device, heartbeat, cochlear implant, prosthetic, 3D printing, scanner, vaccines, drone, paperwork.
• Value: Technology should make healthcare available to everyone.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Ex 1–2 (Preview): Pairs discuss how technology helps us stay healthy and whether everyone in the world has access to it; pairs join into groups and compare.
• Assessment: Check students can give examples and reasons.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book p. 46 (Ex 1–8); Unit 3 video (or the teacher reads the video script aloud if no projector is available); paper for the project; board
Step 1: View for main ideas 10 min
   - Pre-teach prosthetic arm, smartwatch, 3D printing.
   - Ex 3: Watch (or listen to the teacher read the script) and make notes about telemedicine, smartwatches/rings and 3D printing.
Step 2: View for detail 10 min
   - Ex 4: Complete the sentences: 1 travelling, 2 measure, 3 electronic, 4 3D, 5 paperwork, 6 vaccines.
   - Ex 5: Match: 1B, 2C, 3D, 4A.
Step 3: Discussion & project 17 min
   - Ex 6–7: Students make notes on cochlear implants, digital scanners and drones; in groups they decide which is most helpful, and a group leader presents the decision.
   - Ex 8 (Project): Groups think of a health problem and design a new technology to solve it; write a description with at least three reasons it would be useful; present it and hold a class vote.
formative: During the presentations, each listening group writes one question for the presenting group; the teacher checks that answers use clear reasons.
closing: Each student completes: The most useful health technology is … because … .

title: Lesson 8 (Part 1): Unit Check – Review

concepts:
• Grammar: will, be going to, present continuous, present simple for the future; should, ought to, could, Shall …?, How about …?
• Vocabulary: Technology in the home; phrasal verbs; wordlist p. 47.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Wordlist question game: pairs ask each other questions using a word from the wordlist and answer using a different word (Do you have air conditioning? – Yes, and we use it regularly.).
• Assessment: Vocabulary recall and fluency.
activities_teach:
Materials: Student’s Book pp. 47–48 (Wordlist, Practice Ex 1–5, Review Ex 1–6); Audio 3.04, 3.05, 3.06; Grammar file SB pp. 56–57; board
Step 1: Vocabulary practice 12 min
   - Practice Ex 1 (Audio 3.04): 1 washing machine, 2 kettle, 3 air conditioning, 4 coffee maker, 5 fridge-freezer, 6 TV, 7 dishwasher, 8 microwave.
   - Practice Ex 2: Correct the phrasal verbs (Can you turn it down … / Where can I plug my phone in? / Turn it up!).

title: Lesson 8 (Part 2): Workbook – Unit 3 Revision
materials: Workbook p. 35 (Ex 1–6); board
outcomes:
• Complete a conversation with appropriate future forms.
• Find and correct mistakes with future forms and suggestions.
• Use phrasal verbs, advice phrases and unit vocabulary in context.

• Actions: 20 questions: the teacher thinks of a technology from the unit; students ask up to 20 yes/no questions to guess it (Do you use it in the kitchen?).
• Assessment: Question forms and vocabulary.

Materials: Workbook p. 35 (Ex 1–6); board
Step 1: Future forms 14 min
   - Ex 1: 1 are you doing, 2 I’m meeting, 3 Are you going to, 4 I’m going to get, 5 I’ll, 6 I’m not going to, 7 won’t, 8 I’ll pay.

   - Ex 4: 1 plug, 2 came, 3 turn, 4 set, 5 switch, 6 goes, 7 switch, 8 turn.

title: Review: Units 1–3 (Workbook)
materials: Workbook pp. 36–37 (Ex 1–10); Grammar files and wordlists of Units 1–3; board
outcomes:
• Review present tenses, adverbs of frequency, past tenses and future forms in context.
• Recall personality adjectives, adjective + preposition collocations and communication verbs.
• Use technology vocabulary and advice/suggestion phrases accurately.
• Identify personal strengths and weaknesses before the term assessment.
concepts:
• Grammar: Present simple/continuous; adverbs of frequency; past simple/continuous; future forms; advice and suggestions.
• Vocabulary: Personality adjectives, adjective + preposition, communication verbs, technology in the home, phrasal verbs.
pre_learning:
• Actions: Quick quiz on the board: one question from each unit (e.g. I ___ (study) at the moment. / She ___ (talk) when I arrived. / The bus ___ (leave) at 7 tomorrow.). Teams answer on paper.
• Assessment: Identify which unit needs the most revision.
activities_teach:
Materials: Workbook pp. 36–37 (Ex 1–10); Grammar files and wordlists of Units 1–3; board
Step 1: Unit 1 language 12 min
   - Ex 1: 1 study, 2 ’m studying, 3 ’m revising, 4 get up, 5 revise, 6 cycle, 7 do, 8 go, 9 ’m enjoying, 10 ’m learning, 11 also get.
   - Ex 2: 1 of, 2 at, 3 about, 4 with, 5 in, 6 at, 7 at, 8 on, 9 with.
   - Ex 3: 1 shy, confident; 2 sporty, noisy; 3 sociable, clever; 4 funny.
   - Ex 4: Word order, e.g. We often spent our holidays at the beach. / We never took them home.
Step 2: Units 2–3 language 15 min
   - Ex 5: 1 listen to, saying; 2 explain, mean; 3 tell; 4 pronounce, say; 5 understand, talking; 6 translate, means; 7 repeat, hear; 8 listening to, telling.

Step 3: Exam-style tasks 10 min
   - Ex 9 (open cloze): 1 about, 2 to, 3 out, 4 on, 5 at, 6 ’ll.
   - Ex 10 (multiple choice): 1B good at, 2C look up, 3A interested in, 4A translate, 5D explain, 6C means.
formative: Each student fills in a self-assessment table (Unit 1 / 2 / 3: grammar ✓/ ✗, vocabulary ✓/ ✗) based on their errors today and writes one revision target.
closing: Ask: Which unit did you enjoy most and why? Praise students for completing Units 1–3.
